title: National Development Co. v. Triad Holding Corp.
lead: A defendant with homes around the world resisted a default order compelling arbitration because process was left at his New York apartment. The Second Circuit upheld service at that permanently maintained home while he was living there.

actors.name: Triad Holding Corporation
actors.role: Joint-venture company controlled by Adnan Khashoggi

actors.name: Aurora DaSilva
actors.role: Resident housekeeper who accepted federal process

proceedings: 1987 default judgment compelled arbitration; tribunal later made an award.
1989 default confirmed award; district court vacated that judgment but refused to vacate the original arbitration order.
Second Circuit affirmed only the denial of vacatur concerning the 1987 judgment.
limits: Actual notice alone does not cure defective service. Service while absent from this residence expressly reserved. Confirmation judgment and precautionary second confirmation action were outside this appeal.

review.basis: Individually written and compared with the canonical full brief; no new independent opinion audit claimed.

sections.title: A dissolved joint venture leads to ignored arbitration requests
paragraphs: National Development Company, wholly owned by the Philippines, formed the Triad Asia joint venture with Triad Holding Corporation, controlled by Adnan Khashoggi. After dissolution, National Development alleged Khashoggi converted about $3.5 million in assets due to it. The venture agreement required final arbitration under International Chamber of Commerce rules.

In August 1986 National Development requested arbitration and sent notices by registered or certified mail. Receipts returned, including Khashoggi’s. The arbitral organization sent two more copies and received receipts, but nobody responded. Those communications concerned arbitration; receiving them did not itself establish service of a federal summons.

sections.title: Federal process produces two distinct defaults
paragraphs: National Development sued federally to compel arbitration. On December 22, 1986, its process server left the summons and complaint with Aurora DaSilva, a housekeeper at Khashoggi’s Olympic Tower condominium on Fifth Avenue. Khashoggi did not appear, and a September 23, 1987 default ordered arbitration.

The February 1989 arbitration proceeded without defendants. Soon afterward, criminal lawyer Robert Morvillo told the tribunal participation was inadvisable during unrelated pending criminal proceedings. In April the tribunal found Triad Holding Khashoggi’s alter ego and awarded over $3.4 million plus costs, interest, and attorney fees jointly and severally. Those were arbitral findings, not findings the appellate court independently made.

National Development obtained leave for a supplemental confirmation complaint, mailed it to the apartment and Morvillo, and received a second default judgment August 4, 1989. After personal service of discovery later that month, Khashoggi moved in October to vacate both judgments as void for defective service. National Development also filed a precautionary separate confirmation action. Following an evidentiary hearing, District Judge Pollack vacated the 1989 confirmation but preserved the 1987 order compelling arbitration. Only the latter ruling was appealed.

sections.title: The apartment was a maintained home and his current residence
sections.cue: Why domicile did not decide the question
paragraphs: Khashoggi was a Saudi citizen who regarded his six-villa Riyadh compound as his domicile. In 1986 he spent three months there, two months in Spain, and much of the rest traveling among twelve maintained locations, including Rome, Paris, and Monte Carlo. DaSilva testified he stayed at Olympic Tower thirty-four days that year, including December 15–23. The parties stipulated she took the papers December 22, while he was living there.

The apartment exceeded 23,000 square feet on at least two floors, with a pool, sauna, office, furnished guest and brother’s apartments, and two full-time and three part-time staff. Valued around $20–$25 million, it had been purchased in 1974 and remodeled at Khashoggi’s direction for over $1 million. Corporate ownership remained ultimately his, and he called it a residence in a 1989 bail application. These facts established permanence, not minimum wealth or staffing requirements.

DaSilva’s suitable age, discretion, and residence were undisputed. Khashoggi nevertheless argued substituted service was valid only at his Saudi home. The historical federal rule permitted delivery at a dwelling or usual abode to a suitable resident. A person could have several such homes; domicile did not erase where he actually lived.

sections.title: A correct result for a different reason
paragraphs: The district court had thought Olympic Tower was not an abode but treated actual notice as curing service. Judge McLaughlin’s Second Circuit panel rejected that reasoning: knowledge could not cure otherwise void service. Morvillo’s letter cast doubt on Khashoggi’s claimed ignorance until August, but skepticism was no substitute for rule compliance.

The result was nonetheless correct because the apartment qualified as an abode. Permanent maintenance plus Khashoggi’s actual residence when DaSilva accepted process made delivery reasonably calculated to inform him. The court expressly left open whether delivery there during his absence would suffice.

The panel affirmed denial of the motion to vacate the original 1987 default compelling arbitration. It neither reinstated the vacated 1989 confirmation nor decided the second confirmation action or the underlying conversion claim.
